expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: No — that test would not have caught this incident. Walk through why, then what would.

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: The nulls were coalesced to 0 instead of surfaced... This is the data-world equivalent of `except: pass` — it converts a loud failure into a quiet, plausible-looking one.

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: Reconciliation against the source system... Sum of revenue in the warehouse vs. the upstream system's total, with a tolerance.

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: A discusses 'Assert the join match rate before you ever coalesce' but refers to pipeline ordering, not publication gating. No explicit recommendation that assertions block publication before dashboard update.

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: A schema contract on the upstream table... your ingest validates against it and quarantines on mismatch instead of letting a rename flow silently into a join miss.

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: Null-rate assertion on the pre-coalesce join output... Assert the join match rate before you ever coalesce, e.g. fail if >X% of rows are unmatched.

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: Mentions 'three weeks later at close' retrospectively but does not treat the three-week detection latency as a separate gap requiring its own fix.

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: If a revenue join can legitimately have no match, that needs an explicit, named case... not a default that's indistinguishable from 'correctly zero.'
